descripcion: Register is the C1 skill most likely to be invisible to the speaker and obvious to everyone else. Writing to a regulator the way you would write to a colleague is the commonest way advanced speakers misfire. The content is not wrong; the packaging is. Register moves along several axes at once, and the failure is almost always mixing them within one text.

filas: Verbal (*we tested it*) → Nominal (*testing was carried out*)

ejemplos.texto: To a colleague: *This won't scale and we both know it.*
To a manager: *I've got concerns about how this behaves at volume — worth a conversation before we commit.*
In a formal report: *Scalability has not been demonstrated at the volumes anticipated, and further assessment is recommended prior to commitment.*
*Further assessment is recommended prior to commitment.*

notas: Formal English is not harder English; it is a different set.
Over-formalising email reads as cold or sarcastic in most English-speaking workplaces.
Nominalisation raises formality and lowers readability. Use it deliberately, not by default.

es.en: Spanish marks formality heavily through address (*tú/usted*) and verb morphology, which English lacks entirely. English carries the whole load lexically and structurally — so a Spanish speaker who gets the politeness right can still get the register badly wrong.
es.es: El español marca la formalidad de forma intensa mediante el tratamiento («tú/usted») y la morfología verbal, algo que el inglés no tiene. En inglés toda la carga recae en el vocabulario y la estructura, por lo que un hispanohablante puede ser cortés y aun así equivocarse mucho de registro.

de.en: German marks politeness with Sie, which English lacks, so a German speaker who gets the politeness right can still get the register wrong. English carries register through vocabulary, contractions and structure.
de.de: Deutsch markiert Höflichkeit mit «Sie», was dem Englischen fehlt. Daher kann ein deutscher Sprecher höflich sein und trotzdem das Register verfehlen. Im Englischen wird Register über Wortschatz, Kontraktionen und Satzstruktur getragen.

it.en: Italian marks politeness with Lei, which English lacks, so an Italian speaker who gets the politeness right can still get the register wrong. English carries register through vocabulary, contractions and structure.
it.it: L'italiano marca la cortesia con «Lei», che l'inglese non ha. Un italofono può quindi essere cortese e sbagliare comunque registro. In inglese il registro passa attraverso lessico, contrazioni e struttura.

fr.en: French marks politeness with vous, which English lacks, so a French speaker who gets the politeness right can still get the register wrong. English carries register through vocabulary, contractions and structure.
fr.fr: Le français marque la politesse avec «vous», ce que l'anglais n'a pas. Un francophone peut donc être poli tout en se trompant de registre. En anglais, le registre repose sur le vocabulaire, les contractions et la structure.

pt.en: Portuguese marks politeness with você or o senhor, which English lacks, so a Portuguese speaker who gets the politeness right can still get the register wrong. English carries register through vocabulary, contractions and structure.
pt.pt: O português marca a cortesia com «você» ou «o senhor/a senhora», o que o inglês não possui. Assim, um falante de português pode acertar a cortesia e mesmo assim errar o registro. Em inglês, o registro é carregado pelo vocabulário, pelas contrações e pela estrutura.

errores: Register mixing within a paragraph — the commonest real error.
Latinate vocabulary in a message meant to be warm.

es: *Un abrazo* rendered as *A hug* to close a work email instead of *Best* or *Kind regards*.
de: *Mit freundlichen Grüssen* rendered as *With friendly greetings* instead of *Kind regards*.
it: *Un abbraccio* rendered as *A hug* to close a work email instead of *Best* or *Kind regards*.
fr: *Bises* rendered as *Kisses* to close a work email instead of *Best* or *Kind regards*.
pt: *Beijinhos* rendered as *Kisses* to close a work email instead of *Best* or *Kind regards*.

traducciones.es: vivir por encima de las posibilidades
traducciones.it: vivere al di sopra dei propri mezzi

traducciones.fr: nous le savons tous les deux
j’ai des réserves au sujet de

mision.consigna: Write about going into the red three times: a text to a friend, an email to your bank, a formal letter disputing a fee.
requisitos: three texts with no register leak between them
at least two formal markers from the reference box in the letter
the same facts in all three
use *to be in the red*, *fees* and *to live beyond your means*

microtareas.texto: Write *I've got concerns about the fees* in three registers.
Find one register leak in an email you sent this week and fix it.
Record 90 seconds explaining a *nest egg* to a teenager, then 30 seconds to a banker.

autochequeo: Is each version internally consistent across all six axes?
Any contraction in the formal version? Any Latinate chain in the informal one?
Is the content genuinely identical, or did I change the message?
Would each version land with its intended reader?
All four core items across the three?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on register. (1) Rate each of my three versions and say whether it is consistent throughout. (2) Flag every mixed-register sentence. (3) Say which versions would actually land with their reader and which would not. (4) Show me the single word in each version that most gives away its register. Do not rewrite the text.
